[RFCS.23.4] **Fields.** A `FactExternal` carries one field per slot of the
writing schema, in that schema's declaration order, each named for its slot. A
`null` slot is `KIND_NULL`.

**A fact-reference slot carries the referenced fact, inlined** as a nested
`FactExternal` of kind `KIND_FACT_REF`. References are written once, when the
referring fact is asserted ([LGRA.5.7a.2]), so a referenced fact always predates
the fact that refers to it: nesting is finite and acyclic.

**A reference whose target has left working memory is written as `KIND_NULL`,
whether or not the slot is nullable.** The engine holds no copy of the
target to inline. [RFCS.23.7] says how a receiver reads it.

**Nesting is at most 16 deep.** The top-level fact is at depth 0 and a fact
inlined in a slot of a fact at depth *d* is at depth *d* + 1; no inlined fact
may be deeper than 16. A receiving engine must refuse a deeper `FactExternal`
whole, as malformed (`DS_ERR_PARSE`, [NCBK.10.4]). An engine writes a fact
whose references chain deeper as it is, and no receiver accepts it.
